meta.move: Strong path: owns the missed call, then evidence in order, then the rewrite
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so let's not waste the time. Why did my son find out about a zero from his phone, in the middle of class?
Ms. Kalinowski, thank you for coming in. Before anything else: I entered that zero before I called you, and that was wrong. I'm sorry.
Okay. Who decided on the zero, and was anyone going to speak to Owen before it went in?

Here's what I can show you. The document's version history: created at 11:31 PM the night before it was due, title only. At 11:52, 612 words arrive in one edit. At 11:58, another 794. No drafts before that.
I'm writing down 11:31, 11:52 and 11:58. Owen told me he wrote that essay over the weekend, so turn the screen and let me read it myself. Whose account is it, and who else has looked at this?
Second, the essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' That line is not in Hamlet. Here's the scene; you can search it yourself.

I'm writing down that line and the act, and I'll search the text myself. A misquoted line makes a weak essay, Hale, and a weak essay is not a zero. What else do you have besides a timestamp and one sentence?

Our procedure allows a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. We could do it in my room, Thursday at 8:15, with the vice-principal supervising.

I have 4.4 printed, and it says nothing goes on his record. Whatever happens Thursday, it stays quiet and off his file, and I want that in an email from you today. Is the zero out of the gradebook before he sits down, and will anyone from his class be in that room at 8:15?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require the zero withdrawn from the gradebook before any rewrite, written confirmation that nothing goes on Owen's record, and an answer on whether anyone from his class will be in the room. I expect that email from you today.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: the fallback position, with the rewrite offered but not accepted, and she still wants the zero out of the gradebook first, nothing on his record, and the whole thing kept private, all in writing.
What moved her: "that was wrong", because owning the early zero in one sentence and then showing dated documents got her to stop attacking and start asking for terms.
What cost ground: nothing.
Try next time: when you offered the rewrite, say in the same breath that the zero comes out of the gradebook first, since that was the first thing she asked about.
